the distribution of tax revenues is determined by the following factors: (1) federal tax revenues are determined by federal tax revenues, the share of the federal budget in total tax revenues, and the share of the regional budget in the total tax revenues; (2) regional tax revenues are determined only by the share of the region in the federal budget.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the Russian federalism is characterized by endogenous decentralization, which can be explained by the political factors and by the regional differences in the economic development.

the distribution of taxes between the center and the regions is not determined by the traditional factors of federalism but rather by the strategic interaction between the center and regions, and by the institutional and political factors.

the distribution of tax revenues is not a simple result of the fiscal capacity of the regions, but depends on the institutional factors of the federalism and the political preferences of the federal government.
